verses.text: There is another evil I have seen under the sun, and it weighs heavily upon mankind:

xrefs.text: There is a grievous evil I have seen under the sun: wealth hoarded to the harm of its owner,

verses.text: God gives a man riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing his heart desires; but God does not allow him to enjoy them. Instead, a stranger will enjoy them. This is futile and a grievous affliction.

xrefs.text: Furthermore, God has given riches and wealth to every man, and He has enabled him to enjoy them, to accept his lot, and to rejoice in his labor. This is a gift from God.
From their prosperity proceeds iniquity; the imaginations of their hearts run wild.

from such men, O LORD, by Your hand— from men of the world whose portion is in this life. May You fill the bellies of Your treasured ones and satisfy their sons, so they leave their abundance to their children.
Moreover, I will give you what you did not request— both riches and honor— so that during all your days no man in any kingdom will be your equal.
Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.

verses.text: A man may father a hundred children and live for many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he is unsatisfied with his prosperity and does not even receive a proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

xrefs.text: Or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child, like an infant who never sees daylight?
He will be buried like a donkey, dragged away and thrown outside the gates of Jerusalem.
But when they went out to bury her, they found nothing but her skull, her feet, and the palms of her hands.
But better than both is he who has not yet existed, who has not seen the evil that is done under the sun.
But you are cast out of your grave like a rejected branch, covered by those slain with the sword, and dumped into a rocky pit like a carcass trampled underfoot.

verses.text: For a stillborn child enters in futility and departs in darkness, and his name is shrouded in obscurity.

xrefs.text: May his descendants be cut off; may their name be blotted out from the next generation.

verses.text: The child, though neither seeing the sun nor knowing anything, has more rest than that man,

xrefs.text: For that night did not shut the doors of the womb to hide the sorrow from my eyes.
For we are consumed by Your anger and terrified by Your wrath.
Like a slug that dissolves in its slime, like a woman’s stillborn child, may they never see the sun.
[“]Man, who is born of woman, is short of days and full of trouble.

verses.text: even if he lives a thousand years twice over but fails to enjoy his prosperity. Do not all go to the same place?

xrefs.text: Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment,
All go to one place; all come from dust, and all return to dust.
Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.

No longer will they build houses for others to inhabit, nor plant for others to eat. For as is the lifetime of a tree, so will be the days of My people, and My chosen ones will fully enjoy the work of their hands.
Remember that my life is but a breath. My eyes will never again see happiness.

verses.text: All a man’s labor is for his mouth, yet his appetite is never satisfied.

xrefs.text: Do not work for food that perishes, but for food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you. For on Him God the Father has placed His seal of approval.
A worker’s appetite works for him because his hunger drives him onward.
Of course, godliness with contentment is great gain.
Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat or drink; or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothes?

A man may father a hundred children and live for many years; yet no matter how long he lives, if he is unsatisfied with his prosperity and does not even receive a proper burial, I say that a stillborn child is better off than he.

verses.text: What advantage, then, has the wise man over the fool? What gain comes to the poor man who knows how to conduct himself before others?

xrefs.text: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.
The wise man has eyes in his head, but the fool walks in darkness. Yet I also came to realize that one fate overcomes them both.
When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to him and said, “I am God Almighty. Walk before Me and be blameless.
When good things increase, so do those who consume them; what then is the profit to the owner, except to behold them with his eyes?
Instruct those who are rich in the present age not to be conceited and not to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy.

verses.text: Better what the eye can see than the wandering of desire. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.

xrefs.text: I have seen all the things that are done under the sun, and have found them all to be futile, a pursuit of the wind.
If my steps have turned from the path, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if impurity has stuck to my hands,
I saw that all labor and success spring from a man’s envy of his neighbor. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and do good while they live,

Here is what I have seen to be good and fitting: to eat and drink, and to find satisfaction in all the labor one does under the sun during the few days of life that God has given him— for this is his lot.

verses.text: Whatever exists was named long ago, and it is known what man is; but he cannot contend with one stronger than he.

xrefs.text: For He is not a man like me, that I can answer Him, that we can take each other to court.
Woe to him who quarrels with his Maker— one clay pot among many. Does the clay ask the potter, ‘What are you making?’ Does your work say, ‘He has no hands’?
“Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer.”
Why do you complain to Him that He answers nothing a man asks?

And to Adam He said: “Because you have listened to the voice of your wife and have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat, cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life.

verses.text: For the more words, the more futility— and how does that profit anyone?

xrefs.text: There is no limit to all the people who were before them. Yet the successor will not be celebrated by those who come even later. This too is futile and a pursuit of the wind.
For as many dreams bring futility, so do many words. Therefore, fear God.
So I set my mind to know wisdom and madness and folly; I learned that this, too, is a pursuit of the wind.
The wind blows southward, then turns northward; round and round it swirls, ever returning on its course.
Ephraim feeds on the wind and pursues the east wind all day long; he multiplies lies and violence; he makes a covenant with Assyria and sends olive oil to Egypt.

verses.text: For who knows what is good for a man during the few days in which he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow? Who can tell a man what will come after him under the sun?

xrefs.text: You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.
Like a flower, he comes forth, then withers away; like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure.
“The LORD is my portion,” says my soul, “therefore I will hope in Him.”
I have seen that there is nothing better for a man than to enjoy his work, because that is his lot. For who can bring him to see what will come after him?
Man is like a breath; his days are like a passing shadow.
